span.label: Hippocampal phase-locking to auditory input is novelty-dependent, appearing for new stimuli and declining with repetition, which suggests a role in novelty detection.
span.note: WHOSE RESULT THIS IS: studies in guinea pig showed - 2026-08-26 terminal-a. THE SUBJECT OF THIS RESULT IS AN INDEFINITE STUDY, NOT THIS PAPER. `Previous studies reported`, `studies in guinea pig showed`, `recent studies have reported` - somebody else's work under a common noun rather than a name, with a citation in the sentence and no first-person marker. The quote is verbatim and the claim is true; only the attribution is wrong. FOUND BY MEASURING MY OWN CUE'S RECALL: the first sweep required a NAMED author as the subject (`Sperling (1960) demonstrated`) and found 17. Reading eleven citation-bearing findings on `Plakke2016` by hand showed four the cue could not see - `A study examining recognition found`, `studies of typical human subjects have demonstrated`, `A follow up study found` - so the named cue's 17 was a floor and not a count. A CUE'S FALSE POSITIVES TELL YOU NOTHING ABOUT ITS FALSE NEGATIVES, and the only way to find these was to read a record's whole layer. Q-1118.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: 126 dB, 12 kHz narrowband, 2 h — the single acute noise exposure that produced a hippocampal neurogenesis reduction still visible ten weeks later
span.note: WHOSE RESULT THIS IS: pal neurogenesis as seen 10 weeks after exposure (Kraus et al., 2010). - 2026-08-26 terminal-a. THE RESULT IS THE CITED WORK'S AND THE CITATION TRAILS THE SENTENCE. A plain noun phrase is the subject of the result verb and the attribution is a bracket at the end - `Neurons within the dorsal temporal pole demonstrated match suppression ... ( Ng et al., 2014 )`. Neither of my two cues could see this shape, so THESE WERE READ RATHER THAN SWEPT: 36 candidates of the shape, 20 read, 11 marked, 9 refused. THE REFUSALS ARE WHY IT IS NOT A CUE: `Aru2012 findings[16]` is the paper's OWN result with a citation supporting the localisation, `Natan2015 findings[3]` ends `consistent with previous findings ( Szymanski et al., 2009 )` where the main clause is the paper's, and `Drieu2019` x3 are `One cannot entirely rule out...` - a limitation, not an attribution. About 55% precise, which is a list to read and not a sweep to run. NOTE: the cited paper shares this record's first author - a self-citation to earlier work, which is still not THIS paper's result. Q-1119.
